statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits at its floor because the CME equity-index halt leaves no tradable price path; Stress is elevated on a second strike against Saudi energy infrastructure.
recommendation: Path risk is concentrated in the single hour after futures matching resumes at 22:00Z. Outside that window the mapped state remains green with Tail well below the block threshold.
headline: Fourth hour of the Labor Day halt; a fresh Jizan refinery strike lifts Stress while the 22:00Z restart stays the one mapped danger window
body: CME equity-index futures have been halted since 17:00Z and resume matching at 22:00Z for the Tuesday trade date, while NYSE, Nasdaq and the US bond market stayed shut all day for Labor Day and reopen at 13:30Z tomorrow. NQ's last print is unchanged at 29,565.25, up 40.50 points (+0.14%), inside a narrow 29,530.50-29,683.50 holiday range it had already faded from, so the pre-halt tape showed working retracements and no one-way structure. With no order book there is no price path capable of denying mean reversion, which is why Tail sits at its floor; the same absence is what caps a forward read. The material change since the previous hour is a second strike on Saudi energy infrastructure. Aramco's 400,000 barrel-a-day Jizan refinery on the Red Sea coast was hit again on Monday, the second attack there in about a month, with damage still being assessed and no group claiming responsibility. Separately, the CBS live blog carried a late-afternoon update in which the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of airstrikes, including one on a prison that killed seven, with fighting intensifying near the Bab al-Mandab strait. That widening of the theatre is why Stress moves up a point to 63. It does not move Tail, because the price evidence points the other way: WTI October futures closed at 91.48, up only 0.20%, after reaching 93.29 intraday, and Brent is near 96.94, up 0.69%, having touched 97.93 earlier, its highest since 23 July. Crude retraced from its highs on the same day the escalation headlines landed, which is orderly two-way discovery rather than a one-way impulse. A partial counterweight is that Iran's talks with Oman on new Hormuz transit routes are described as being in their final stages, with passage maps expected to be signed in the coming days. Set against that, Iran's plan to declare a maritime exclusion zone running from the US naval blockade line toward the Strait remains announced intent rather than an executed action, and Hormuz transits are down to roughly ten vessels a day against about 130 before the war. The macro backdrop is a separate and independent channel. Friday's August payrolls came in at 162,000 against roughly 55,000 expected with unemployment at 4.1%, pushing odds of a September Fed rate increase to about 58% and lifting the two-year yield to its highest since January 2025; the Dow fell 0.51%, the S&P 500 0.38% to 7,718.60 and the Nasdaq Composite 0.29% to 26,506.99. US Treasury cash markets were closed today, so the most recent H.15 values remain those for 3 September, 4.34% at two years and 4.77% at ten. VIX last traded near 15.30, historically calm. The latest completed equity session showed unusually wide internal dispersion, with semiconductors broadly higher against sharp declines in several megacaps, which is a Stress and Confidence input rather than a Tail amplifier. The single concentrated risk is the 22:00Z restart, where roughly five hours of unpriced escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the week. That hour alone is mapped to WATCH; path risk then decays through Asia and rises again modestly into the 13:30Z cash reopen. All post-halt structure is described conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail confined to a 5-10% band. Stress ran at 54-57% through the Asian and European sessions, rose to 61-64% across the US afternoon as crude extended and holiday liquidity thinned, and has held at 62% since the halt. Confidence fell from 86% to 75% over the stretch as live price evidence disappeared with the 17:00Z halt. Dominant mode was normal apart from the 14:00Z, 16:00Z and 17:00Z slots, which were mixed while the energy-versus-equity divergence widened.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are governed by market structure rather than macro. Futures stay halted for another hour and a half, so the opening forecast slots carry no tradable path and Tail sits at its floor. The one elevated slot is the 22:00Z restart, where several hours of unpriced escalation, now including a second strike on Aramco's Jizan refinery and Iran's announced intent to declare a Hormuz-area exclusion zone, would meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; that hour alone maps to WATCH. Path risk then decays through the Asian and European sessions as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend and the first full-depth pricing of both the weekend tanker exchange and Friday's hawkish payroll surprise. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff; only the pre-halt range, its fade, and crude's retracement from its session highs are stated as fact. NFIB at 10:00Z and the weekly ADP print at 12:15Z are the only scheduled US releases inside the window, with the 3-year auction at 17:00Z as a rates checkpoint and PPI and claims on Thursday and CPI on Friday as the week's principal events.
